newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican bank chief mulls hiring ex-Salinas aide.
newsitem.headline: Mexican bank chief mulls hiring ex-Salinas aide.

text.p: The head of Mexico's largest banking group Banamex-Accival was considering hiring one of the most controversial figures of the disgraced presidency of Carlos Salinas, banking sources said on Thursday.
Sources said bank chief Roberto Hernandez and his colleague, Alfredo Harp Helu, were in talks with Salinas' former chief of staff Jose Cordoba Montoya to employ him as an adviser.

"He wouldn't come as an adviser to the group or the bank, he would be an adviser on a personal basis in areas that have still not been defined, to Roberto Hernandez and Alfredo Harp," a source at the bank, known as Banacci, told Reuters.

Cordoba was widely revered as the power behind Salinas's 1988-1994 presidency but plunged into disgrace alongside his former boss when Mexico sank into a deep economic crisis just weeks after Salinas left office.
Still admired abroad, Cordoba was Mexico's representative at the Inter-American Development Bank in Washington after leaving the presidency, a post he has since relinquished.

If Salinas, living in self-imposed exile in Ireland, was Mexico's public enemy No. 1, Cordoba was widely considered the No. 2. Last October he was forced to defend himself from insinuations in Congress that he helped plot the assassination of a former presidential candidate.
He was also questioned by prosecutors investigating the 1994 murder of the candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio.
Bank analysts expressed alarm that Cordoba, if hired, could taint the banking group.

But the Banacci source stressed the relationship would be a personal one with Hernandez and Harp. Both men soared to prominence during Salinas' rule, winning the privatisation of Banamex, Mexico's largest and most coveted bank.
